name: 260. Zero-key custom provider does not hijack provider inference (keyless provider inference)
description: A custom provider with no keys that is not marked is_key_less used to be treated as serving every model. Provider inference for a bare model sorts candidates by name, so such a provider (every custom provider starts with zero keys until one is added, and the harness leaves several pointed at dead base URLs) won the pick over the real provider; its key pool then failed with 400 no_key_supports_model, which counted as a caller error, so the inferred fallbacks never ran. Seen as /openai/v1/embeddings {model: text-embedding-005} answered by harness-oauthkey-run-... instead of Vertex. The fix: only a keyless provider is unrestricted with zero keys, and no_key_supports_model no longer stops an inferred fallback chain. Rows: (1) create a zero-key, non-keyless openai-based custom provider whose name sorts before vertex; (2) the bare-model embedding is served by vertex, not by it; (3) delete it. Red before the fix: row 2 returns 400 no_key_supports_model naming the harness provider. Run with FEATURE="keyless provider inference".

item.name: 260.1 vertex/text-embedding-005 setup: create a zero-key custom provider that sorts before vertex (keyless provider inference)

exec: pm.test('created the zero-key provider', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.eql(200); });

item.name: 260.2 vertex/text-embedding-005 bare model on /openai/v1/embeddings is served by vertex, not the zero-key provider (keyless provider inference)
